anomalies.observed: Both ground pins on each isolated CAN transceiver are connected to the same GND net: U20.4 (GND1) and U20.5 (GND2), and U47.4 (GND1) and U47.5 (GND2).
anomalies.expected: The CAN transceivers' logic-side and bus-side grounds should remain separate to preserve the specified galvanic isolation.
anomalies.impact: Tying the transceivers' grounds together bypasses their isolation barriers. The CAN links may still communicate, but they lose the intended galvanic isolation and its protection against ground-potential differences and ground-loop currents.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present: both isolated CAN transceivers have their logic-side and bus-side ground pins tied to the same GND net. This defeats the specified galvanic isolation on both CAN interfaces.
